steps.title: Sign in to Spotify (any Spotify account)
steps.notes: The dashboard URL redirects once to accounts.spotify.com/en/login with a continue= parameter that returns to developer.spotify.com/loggedin. The wall offers email, phone number, Google, Facebook and Apple sign-in, plus Sign up. The page footer says it is protected by reCAPTCHA. No cookie banner seen on the login page. The signed-in account is the app owner, so it must be the account that has Premium (see step 3).

steps.title: Open the Dashboard and click Create an App
steps.quote: You can create up to 25 apps per developer account
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The screenshot of the docs' Create app dialog shows fields App name, App description, Website, Redirect URI, a checklist of which APIs/SDKs you plan to use, and the terms checkbox. Whether the dashboard asks for anything extra on a first visit (developer terms, email verification) was not seen: UNCERTAIN for that part.

steps.title: Check the owner account has Spotify Premium
steps.quote: The app owner must have a Spotify Premium account for apps in development mode to function
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. If the owner account is Free, the human has to subscribe or use a Premium account before the app will work. The docs do not say whether the dashboard blocks creation for a Free account, so the creation-time behavior is UNCERTAIN.

steps.title: Fill in App name, App description and Website
steps.quote: put a tick in the Developer Terms of Service checkbox
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The docs say the name and description are displayed to users on the grant screen, so use customer-facing wording. Agent can prepare the values; a human types them in.

steps.title: Set the Redirect URI to Composio's callback
steps.quote: Use HTTPS for your redirect URI, unless you are using a loopback address, when HTTP is permitted
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Value to paste: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback (per Composio docs; copy the exact value shown in your Composio auth config, since some toolkits still show a legacy URL). It is HTTPS, so it passes Spotify's rule. The match must be exact: 'The definition of the redirect URI must exactly match the redirect URI you provide when you create your app' (verified). Separate verified rule: 'localhost is not allowed as redirect URI'; use http://127.0.0.1:PORT or http://[::1]:PORT for local testing. The cookie banner partly covers the localhost bullet in the screenshot, so the quote check is the evidence for it.

steps.title: Select the API: tick Web API; accept the terms; click Save
steps.quote: put a tick in the Developer Terms of Service checkbox
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. The docs text says 'click on CREATE' while the docs screenshot shows a Save button, so the label has drifted; the screenshot is of the docs image, not the live form. The app appears immediately in development mode, with no approval step.

steps.title: Know the development-mode limits (5 users, allowlist)
steps.quote: Up to 5 authenticated Spotify users can use an app that is in development mode
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Also verified: 'Each Spotify user who installs your app will need to be added to your app's allowlist before they can use it'. Allowlist path in the docs: Dashboard > app > Settings > Users Management > Add new user (name and Spotify email). Request quotas also apply to development mode apps, with a 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED response; groupings are said to be subject to change.

steps.title: Copy Client ID and Client Secret into a Composio auth config
steps.quote: Client Secret, the key you will use to authorize your Web API or SDK calls
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page; the docs say these appear on the app overview page and that a ROTATE button regenerates the secret. The overview page itself needs sign-in and was not seen. Exact secret reveal behavior (a click to show it) is UNCERTAIN.

steps.title: Optional: apply for extended quota to go beyond 5 users
steps.quote: Spotify only accepts applications from organizations (not individuals)
steps.notes: Quote verified on the live page. Also verified: requirements include 'Maintaining a minimum of active users (at least 250k MAUs)', and 'This review process can take up to six weeks'. In practice this makes extended quota out of reach for individuals and small apps, so a Composio user should plan for development mode (5 allowlisted users) unless they are an established organization. Application goes through a company-email form, then a quota extension request tab in the dashboard. Not tested beyond the docs.

blocked_at.what_it_asks_for: A Spotify account: email, phone, or Google / Facebook / Apple sign-in. Page notes reCAPTCHA protection.

observations: Console wall reached in one redirect; no waitlist or approval in front of the dashboard as far as visible.

The real blocker for production use is not app creation but the quota rules: development mode allows 5 allowlisted users and needs a Premium owner, and extended quota is organizations only with a 250k MAU bar.
Redirect URIs: HTTPS is fine (Composio's callback qualifies); localhost is explicitly rejected, so local testing needs 127.0.0.1 or [::1].
Docs page for the Create dialog uses a screenshot image, not text, for the field list; the 'CREATE' button name in the text does not match the 'Save' button in the image.
The cookie banner is a fixed overlay that covers part of the capture on two docs shots and could not be moved out of the way by changing --find.
Fifteen of fifteen quotes tried were verified on the live page.
